title: India's Top Judge Calls Viral Casteist Quote a Fake
excerpt: CJI Surya Kant issues a rare personal denial, threatening legal action against X account that spread fabricated remarks
body:
India's Chief Justice Surya Kant fired back on May 9 against a social media campaign falsely attributing a casteist Hindi-language quote to him, calling the fabrication a 'vile, brazen and mischievous' concoction in a statement to PTI.

**What Happened:**
A fabricated casteist statement was falsely attributed to the CJI on social media — specifically by the X account @UnreservedMERIT, which circulated a graphic carrying the quote alongside a photograph of the Chief Justice captioned 'Chief Justice of India.' The post garnered over 16,900 views before the Office of the CJI intervened. CJI Surya Kant categorically denied making any such statement, saying the assertions were 'entirely baseless and do not reflect my words, views, or character.'

**Why It Matters:**
The CJI stated that 'to manufacture a fictitious quote, and to attribute it to the highest judicial office of the land, is an act of rank dishonesty, deliberate social incitement, and contempt for constitutional values,' warning that 'such reckless conduct strikes at the very foundation of public trust in the judiciary and the rule of law.' He made clear he will 'bring the full might of the law' against those behind the viral post. The Office of the CJI also called upon 'all responsible citizens, media organisations, and social media platforms to refrain from amplifying false and contrived content.'

**What to Watch:**
Whether India's law enforcement agencies pursue criminal proceedings against the @UnreservedMERIT account — and whether X complies with any takedown or identification requests — will set a significant precedent for accountability over judicially targeted misinformation.
nri_angle: Indian-Americans who consume Hindi-language social media content or follow India's Supreme Court closely may have encountered this fabricated quote, making the CJI's official denial essential context before sharing or reacting.
